Title: Tokyo Castle: Imperial Palace, Shogun & Garden Walking Tour
Description:
Join one of Tokyo’s highest rated walking tours! Together we will explore the Imperial Palace and its beautiful Eastern Gardens with our super friendly local guide :)
You won’t just hear about Japan’s history, you’ll feel it come alive through stories, humor, and moments that make this place unforgettable :)
Our guides are known for their warmth, energy, and genuine passion for sharing Tokyo’s past, that’s why our guests keep calling this tour “the highlight of their trip!”

We’ll begin at Wadakura Fountain Park with riverside views and the surrounding moats, then stroll to Ōtemon Gate and you will learn the story behind the castle gates and their role in Japan’s samurai past!

From there we’ll explore historic guardhouses and ruins, stopping at amazing photo spots that most visitors miss!

Next, we’ll walk through the beautiful Ninomaru Garden!
Its winding paths, seasonal flowers, ponds and imperial koi fish (can only be found here!) are perfect for a calm break from the city :)

Along the way our guide will bring to life how the Shogun’s world shaped modern Japan (!) and tell stories of the Edo era you won’t find on any plaque!

Our guides are the number 1 thing that makes this tour special: friendly, energetic, and full of stories and practical tips! <3

They love answering questions and will give other recommendations to deepen your stay in Tokyo, so please do not hesitate to ask :)

Whether you’re here for history, the gardens, or just want a deeper connection to Japanese culture, this tour is perfect for you!

Our small group tours make it easy to ask questions to your guide about anything in Tokyo (doesn’t have to be tour related).

Whether you’re a couple, family, or traveling solo, we want you to leave with a real sense of the Palace’s history, gardens, and local traditions :)

We look forward to welcoming you on this tour!

Title: Hakone: Self Guided Trip to Mt. Fuji // Made by Local Guides
Description:
IMPORTANT INFO: 

After purchasing this tour, you will receive an e-mail with the PDF of your itinerary. Please give us 1-3 business days to get back to you as we have a lot of emails to go through, but rest assured that we will get back to you as fast as we can! :)  

About the tour: 

Our comprehensive guide is your passport to exploring the wonders of Mt. Fuji with ease and confidence. From transportation options and insider tips to must-see attractions and hidden gems, we've curated every detail to ensure a seamless and enriching experience. Say goodbye to the stress of planning and hello to adventure!   Get ready for an action-packed day of exploration! Here's a sneak peek at what awaits you:  - 

Begin your journey from Shinjuku station (in Tokyo) and head for; Moto Hakone, a quaint village nestled amidst lush greenery. Immerse yourself in its charming streets lined with traditional shops and eateries. Don't forget to snap some photos of the stunning scenery!  - 

Next stop, Amazake Chaya, a hidden gem known for its delicious traditional treats. Indulge your taste buds with warm amazake (sweet rice wine) and savory snacks while soaking in the cozy atmosphere of this historic teahouse.  - 

Step back in time as you board the Old Tokaido Line, a historic railway route that once connected Tokyo and Kyoto. Marvel at the scenic views from your window seat as you journey through picturesque landscapes and quaint villages.  - 

Prepare for a thrilling voyage across Lake Ashi aboard a majestic pirate ship! Feel the wind in your hair and the excitement in the air as you cruise along the tranquil waters, with Mt. Fuji towering majestically in the distance. Keep your camera ready for postcard-perfect views!  - 

Conclude your day at the stunning Mount Owakudano, where natural beauty and culinary delights await. Ascend to the summit for breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Fuji and the surrounding landscape. 

Then, treat yourself to the famous black onsen eggs, boiled in the geothermal waters of Owakudani. Legend has it that each egg adds seven years to your life – talk about a tasty bonus!

Title: Tokyo: A Traditional Japanese Tea Ceremony with a Tea Master
Description:
Step into the heart of Japanese tradition at the Ocharu Tea Ceremony, right across from Tokyo University. This is more than just a tea ceremony—it's a vibrant journey through Japan’s rich tea culture.

Start with a refreshing cup of wakocha, a unique Japanese black tea from Shizuoka, paired with a delicious tea cake. This blend of fruity and floral notes sets the stage for the experience ahead.

Then, watch as a master brews Gyokuro sencha, the highest grade of green tea. Taste the tea leaves and savor seasonal wagashi sweets from “Ougiya,” a renowned confectioner that has been creating these treats for generations.

Next, you’ll whisk your own matcha under the guidance of a skilled tea master. Using traditional tools, you’ll make and enjoy matcha that connects you to centuries of Japanese tea culture.

Finish your experience with a soothing cup of Genmaicha, a blend of sencha and roasted rice from Niigata Prefecture, providing a comforting end to your tea journey.

Before you leave, get a certificate and a group photo to remember your dive into Japan’s tea culture!

Title: Tokyo: Asakusa Temple & Shrine Walking Tour with Local Guide
Description:
Come with us on this small group walking tour through Asakusa and Tokyo´s oldest Temple!

We’ll begin at the Azumabashi Bridge with riverside views of the Tokyo Skytree to see the golden poop (yes that is what the locals call it), then head to the top of the Asakusa Tourist Information Center for a hidden view point of the entire Temple area!

From there, we’ll enter the famous Kaminarimon Gate, where you’ll learn the story behind its 700kg red lantern and the meaning of its name; "The Thunder Gate."

As we walk through Nakamise shopping street, your guide will share the cultural significance behind the treats and souvenirs, as well as where to find the good stuff!

If you need any help with translations, just ask our guide :)

But the real heart of the tour lies in what most visitors miss: tucked away shrines and temple sites that reveal the complex spiritual life of Japan!

You’ll see how Shinto (Japanese religion) and Buddhism coexist, how rituals like temizu hand washing and omikuji fortune telling works, and why locals burn incense for healing, both physically and mentally.

All of this you will also get to do together with your guide, and its fun rituals we recommend everyone to do as a cultural experience :)

Inside the Sensoji Temple itself, you’ll learn how to properly pray in the Buddhist style , a different process than at the neighboring Shinto Asakusa Shrine (where you will also get to go).

You'll even learn how to bow the correct way, walk on the correct side through the torii gates, and learn what even most Japanese people don’t realize about their own mix of traditions!

Whether you’re here for the history, the rituals, or just want a deeper connection with Japanese culture, this tour is perfect for you!

We want everyone to feel comfortable, so please wear whatever you like, tattoos are welcome, and there is no dress code!

Our small-group tours make it easy to ask questions to your guide about anything in Tokyo (dosent have to be tour related).

Whether you are a couple, family, or traveling solo, we want you to leave Asakusa with a real sense of its culture, history, and local traditions :)

We look forward to welcome you on this tour! :)

Title: Tokyo : Visite à Pied Asakusa & Sensoji (GUIDE FRANÇAIS)
Description:
Rejoignez-nous pour cette visite guidée à pied en petit groupe à travers Asakusa et le plus ancien temple de Tokyo !


Nous commencerons par le pont Azumabashi, d'où nous pourrons admirer la Tokyo Skytree depuis les berges, puis nous nous dirigerons vers le toit du Centre d'Information Touristique d'Asakusa pour profiter d'un point de vue caché sur l'ensemble du quartier du temple !


De là, nous passerons la célèbre porte Kaminarimon, où vous découvrirez l'histoire  qui se cache derrière sa lanterne rouge de 700 kg et la signification de son nom, « la Porte du Tonnerre ». 


En parcourant la rue commerçante Nakamise, votre guide vous fera découvrir la signification culturelle des friandises et des souvenirs, ainsi que les meilleurs endroits où les trouver !

Si vous avez besoin d'aide pour la traduction, n'hésitez pas à demander à notre guide :)


Mais le véritable intérêt de la visite réside dans ce que la plupart des visiteurs manquent : les sanctuaires et temples cachés qui révèlent la complexité de la vie spirituelle au Japon ! 

Vous découvrirez comment le Shintoïsme (religion japonaise) et le Bouddhisme coexistent, comment fonctionnent les rituels tels que le nettoyage des mains Temizu et la divination Omikuji, et pourquoi les habitants brûlent de l'encens pour se soigner, tant physiquement que mentalement. 

Vous pourrez également participer à toutes ces activités avec votre guide, et nous recommandons à tout le monde de s'adonner à ces rituels amusants comme expérience culturelle :) 

À l’intérieur du temple Sensō-ji, vous apprendrez la manière appropriée de prier selon le rituel bouddhiste, différent de celui pratiqué au sanctuaire shintō voisin d’Asakusa, que vous visiterez également.

Vous apprendrez même à vous incliner correctement, à passer du bon côté des portes torii et à découvrir des petites facettes de ces traditions que même la plupart des Japonais ignorent !


Que vous soyez ici pour l'histoire, les rituels ou simplement pour approfondir votre connaissance de la culture japonaise, cette visite est faite pour vous.


Nous voulons que tout le monde se sente à l'aise, alors portez ce que vous voulez, les tatouages sont les bienvenus et il n'y a pas de code vestimentaire !


Nos visites en petits groupes vous offrent l’occasion de poser toutes vos questions à votre guide, que ce soit sur Tokyo ou sur tout autre sujet. Que vous veniez en couple, en famille ou en solo, notre objectif est que vous quittiez Asakusa avec une vraie compréhension de sa culture, de son histoire et de ses traditions locales :)

Nous avons hâte de vous accueillir pour cette visite !

Passing through towering wooden gates, we enter the vast forest of Meiji Jingu Shrine, built in 1920 to honor Emperor Meiji.

Along the way, we’ll also explore Omotesando, an avenue inspired by European style, and talk about how Western influence reshaped Tokyo in the Meiji era. From modern pop culture to imperial traditions, this walk reveals how Tokyo lives in both the present and the past at the same time.

Then we’ll enter the tranquil forest surrounding Meiji Shrine. Inside the shrine grounds you’ll learn proper shrine etiquette and the cleansing ritual at the hand washing basin, all explained and practiced together with the guide so you can try it the right way :)
